claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT incorporating a Hubbard U correction will predict a ferromagnetic ground state in transition-metal compounds.
Exchange-correlation interactions stabilize parallel spin alignments.
The initial material is a high-temperature or itinerant electronic phase without observed magnetic ordering.
A Hubbard U parameter accounts for strong on-site Coulomb interactions in first-principles calculations.
Electronic correlations are pronounced under the proposed low-temperature conditions.
The relevant crystal structure supports localized magnetic moments.
Octahedral or tetrahedral coordination promotes localization of transition-metal d electrons.
Spin-polarized calculations stabilize exchange splitting between spin-up and spin-down states.
The Hubbard U term enhances electron localization.
Enhanced localization favors cooperative parallel spin alignment by reducing the electron-delocalization energy cost.
The proposed mechanism lowers the total energy of the ferromagnetic state relative to nonmagnetic or antiferromagnetic states.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have lower computed total energy than competing configurations.
Finite magnetic moments will be predicted at transition-metal sites.
DFT without spin polarization or without Hubbard U typically does not reliably capture ferromagnetic stabilization.
The prediction is most applicable to compounds with intermediate-to-strong electronic correlations.
Weakly correlated or strongly itinerant materials may not exhibit a strong calculated energetic preference for ferromagnetism.
The selected Hubbard U value can significantly affect calculated energy differences and magnetic moments.
The magnitudes of the energy difference and magnetic moments cannot be specified reliably without calibration against experiment.
Low-temperature SQUID magnetometry can test the predicted magnetic ordering.
Failure to obtain a lower-energy ferromagnetic configuration, or experimental observation inconsistent with ferromagnetic ordering, would falsify the hypothesis.
